Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mean verb

signify

also meaning, what does it mean?, stand for, refer to

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.88: carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs
Traupman 30

significō, significāre, significāvī, significātum

verb, first conjugation

mean, signify (of a word or a sign)

With the word or sign as subject: Quid hoc verbum significat? Lewis & Short: of words, “to mean, import, signify”.

Examples

  • Quid volt sibi, Syre, haec ōrātiō?

    What does this talk mean, Syrus?Ter. Heaut. 615

  • carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs

    So “to lack” means this: to be without what you would like to have.Cic. Tusc. 1.88

  • plēraque sunt vocābula quibus vulgō ūtimur, neque tamen liquidō scīmus quid ea propriē atque vērē significent

    There are many words we use every day without knowing clearly what they properly and truly mean.Gell. 16.5.1

  • Quid hoc verbum significat?

    What does this word mean?composed

Other words

  • valeō, valēre, valuī — of a word: mean, have the force of

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.39: hoc verbum quid valeat, nōn vident; Cic. Fin. 2.13: quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat

    Idem valet: it means the same.

  • quid sibi vult? — what does it mean? (of words, things and doings)

    also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 615: Quid volt sibi, Syre, haec ōrātiō?; Cic. Sen. 65: avāritia vērō senīlis quid sibi velit, nōn intellegō; Traupman 103: quid hoc sibi vult?

    From sibi velle, “want for oneself”; of a person, “what is he after?” (see mean, intend).

  • dīcō, dīcere, dīxī, dictum — mean (someone or something), refer to

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.1 (Lewis & Short): Platōnem vidēlicet dīcis; Traupman 103: scīsne quem dīcam?

    Of the speaker: Quem dīcis?, “Who do you mean?” Lewis & Short: “to mean so and so”.

  • significātiō, significātiōnis f. — meaning (of a word)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. LL 9.40; Cic. Part. Or. 108; Quint. 9.1.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 30; M-O s.v. meaning (of a word)

    Also vīs, the force of a word (M-O). Sēnsus for the sense of a word is poetic and post-Augustan (Ov., Quint.).

See also mean, word, understand, language, mention.
